_comment: The bean graph. `beans/` is a graph whose DIRECTORIES are declared here — the same shape as `cat-harness.json`, reusing `ContentDirectorySchema` and the same open graph-kind registry rather than a parallel vocabulary. `graphs` is an array because a directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does NOT say how to tell the contents apart, because the files declare what they are (a bean's front matter, a workflow instance's `$schema`). Paths resolve against THIS file's directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. Schema: schemas/bean-graph.ts. NOTE: `.beans.yml` still carries the defs path because the `beans` binary is third-party; `bun run check:harness-dirs` fails when they disagree.
name: folio-assistant

directories.description: Work items — one Markdown file each, in the layout the `beans` CLI reads.

The same kind as `defs`, moved aside. Bean `e8m3`: the owner ruled 2026-09-26 that archiving is a VIEW rather than a terminal state, so an archived bean keeps its status and is still part of the store. Declared because it holds 631 bean-defs and nothing declared it — a present-but-undeclared directory, which the directory checks cannot see because they compare declarations against disk and not the reverse. `check:bean-archive` holds the invariant the ruling implies: every bean in here is terminal, because a non-terminal one is open work invisible to every count.

One pull request's addendum to a bean, in a file of its own: `<bean>--<date>--<branch>.md`, so two pull requests adding to one bean never write one path. `README.md` is the generated index (`bun run beans:notes`). Bean `m61r`, issue #1853.
Running BPMN instances — one JSON file each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-workflow-instance/v1"`.

A merge steward's decisions about open pull requests — one JSON file each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-merge-queue-entry/v1"`. Beside `workflows/` deliberately: this holds the DECISIONS (priority, hold, ejection, the train joined, each with its reason), and a finished train run under `workflows/` holds the EVIDENCE those decisions met. A reader asking why one pull request went into a given train needs both, and should look in one store. It records no fact GitHub owns — CI, mergeability, labels and the head SHA are read live at decision time and refused by name in the schema, because a stored copy is a second answer that goes stale on the next push. Bean `hfag`.

Published surveys of commit windows. Bean `6ptx`: eight sessions surveyed the same ~2435-commit window in one minute and that day produced ONE authored commit. Each file records the window's TWO EDGE COMMITS, so a later session computes the uncovered delta rather than re-deriving the whole range — staleness decidable, not guessed.
